name: Quicken Classic Deluxe
tagline: Maintain a local personal ledger with imports, budgets, and reports

pricing.notes: Annual subscription converted to a monthly equivalent; promotions vary.

tiers.name: Classic Deluxe
tiers.limits: Multiple budgets; debt tools; tax reports; retirement planner; investment tracking; unlimited tags/custom categories
tiers.notes: Displayed price is a first-year promotional monthly equivalent, billed annually; offer ends 2026-09-11.

tiers.name: Classic Deluxe + LifeHub
tiers.limits: Classic Deluxe plus LifeHub document and essential-information organization
tiers.notes: First-year promotional monthly equivalent, billed annually; bundle page shows a regular comparison price of $10.98/month equivalent.

pricing.billingTerms: annual only; full annual charge upfront; first-year promotional pricing
pricing.hiddenCosts: Auto-renews yearly at the then-current rate, which is not numerically disclosed on the page. Third-party terms/fees may apply. Product is designed for the US and Canada.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Quicken Classic Deluxe, maintain a local personal ledger with imports, budgets, and reports. The hard boundary is bank downloads, investment support, tax reports, long history, and desktop support, plus financial integrations, compliance, and trust.
coreLoopDIY: Maintain a local personal ledger, import transactions, categorize them with transparent rules, reconcile balances, and export budgets and reports without moving money.
requirements: CSV or OFX exports from financial institutions
whatYouLose: bank downloads, investment support, tax reports, long history, and desktop support
replacementScope: personal ledger or simple invoicing tool
ongoingBurden: import normalization, reconciliation, rule drift, exchange rates, backups, audit trails, tax changes, bank APIs, and support
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Quicken Classic Deluxe because people pay because accurate money records and dependable institution connections are worth more than the visible charts. The recurring cost buys import normalization, reconciliation, rule drift, exchange rates, backups, audit trails, tax changes, bank APIs, and support, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Actual Budget
priorArt.desc: Active local-first open-source personal finance application.

alternatives.name: Money Manager Ex
alternatives.desc: A local ledger with imports, budgets, reports and investments; the interface has no subscription budget.

facts.install: Native or portable desktop package for Windows, macOS, or Linux; mobile builds are also published
facts.dataFormat: Accounts and transactions live in a user-chosen local SQLite .mmb database, with optional database encryption; CSV, QIF, and other interchange formats are available.
facts.gapVsPaid: Money Manager Ex covers the ledger but has thinner bill-management, investment analysis, tax-oriented reporting, online-service integration, and commercial support than Quicken Classic.

alternatives.name: GnuCash
alternatives.desc: Industrial-strength local books, imports, budgets and reports; usability is an elective.

facts.install: Native desktop installer or operating-system package
facts.dataFormat: The default book is a local compressed XML .gnucash file; SQLite, MySQL, and PostgreSQL backends are optional, but the documentation warns that database storage does not make GnuCash a true multi-user application.
facts.gapVsPaid: GnuCash is less approachable and gives up Quicken's guided bill, investment, tax-reporting, online account, and support workflow even though the underlying ledger is capable.

alternatives.name: KMyMoney
alternatives.desc: A local ledger with imports, budgets, investments and forecasts; the desktop still believes in menus.

facts.install: Install a distribution package, Flatpak/AppImage, or the published Windows/macOS desktop build
facts.dataFormat: The normal .kmy file is compressed XML on the user's disk and can be GPG-encrypted; KMyMoney also supports SQL storage and imports such as QIF, OFX, and GnuCash XML.
facts.gapVsPaid: KMyMoney's platform-dependent online banking and investment workflow are less consistent, and its reporting and bill-management polish trail Quicken Classic.

alternatives.name: Actual Budget
alternatives.desc: Imports, envelope budgets and reports on your disk; investment tracking is basic.

facts.install: Native desktop app for local-only use, or the official Docker/Node server for browser access and device sync
facts.dataFormat: Each client works from a local SQLite budget; the server keeps account metadata plus budget blobs under its data directory, and optional end-to-end encryption covers budget contents but not bank-sync tokens.
facts.gapVsPaid: Actual is excellent for envelope budgeting but materially thinner than Quicken Classic for investments, tax reports, loan and bill management, and traditional personal-finance reporting.

alternatives.name: Wealthfolio
alternatives.desc: Local investments, spending, budgets and reports; traditional bill-pay features are thinner.

facts.install: Native desktop or iOS app, or the official Docker image/Compose deployment for web mode
facts.dataFormat: Desktop and self-hosted modes use a local SQLite database (the web server exposes a configurable app.db path); optional Wealthfolio Connect and encrypted device sync send selected holdings/account data through the vendor service.
facts.gapVsPaid: Wealthfolio is investment-first and lacks Quicken Classic's mature bill management, account reconciliation, tax categories, loan tools, and broad personal-ledger reporting.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Classic Deluxe plan and a personal ledger or simple invoicing tool DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Quicken Classic Deluxe in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, SQLite, Drizzle ORM, and local-first encryption; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: maintain a local personal ledger, import transactions, categorize them with transparent rules, reconcile balances, and export budgets and reports without moving money.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Support CSV and OFX import with saved column mappings and duplicate detection.
Implement accounts, transactions, transfers, categories, payees, notes, and split transactions.
Add deterministic categorization rules whose matches can be inspected and undone.
Provide reconciliation, monthly budget, cash-flow, net-worth, and export views.
Keep an immutable import log and require explicit confirmation before destructive changes.
Encrypt local data, create automatic backups, and document restore on a fresh machine.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out initiating payments or moving money.
Deliberately leave out tax, payroll, or accounting compliance guarantees.
Deliberately leave out screen-scraped bank access and commercial institution aggregation.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
